answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may submit bids, with voting weight capped per verified stake tier rather than per account. Splitting one balance across a thousand sybils then creates no extra influence: the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, paying opportunity cost and risking slashing for provable fraud. A reef of independent agents can compare claims, while a falcon watches for coordinated timing and a prism separates shared funding patterns from genuinely distinct participants.
